title: Review: The Sneaker Store
setup:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("sneakers.csv")
explanation: Level 1 review! This is a sneaker store, the same one from the SQL course. df already holds sneakers.csv: each row is one shoe, with its brand, category, release year, price and how many are in stock. No new ideas here, just everything from Level 1: loading and peeking, shape and describe(), picking columns, lists and dictionaries.

lines.explain: Pick the name and brand columns, then show the first 3 rows.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: what will this print?
hints: shape is (rows, columns). Count the shoes.

tasks.prompt: Show the name, brand and price of the last 3 shoes.

solution_lines.explain: Pick 3 columns, then show the last 3 rows.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: what is the average (mean) price shown by this summary?
hints: The mean is the average: add all prices and divide by 12.
The prices add up to 1,485. 1,485 ÷ 12 is just under 124.

solution_lines.explain: describe() works on a single column too. The mean price is 123.75. (65 is the cheapest shoe and 190 the most expensive.)

tasks.prompt: Rename the stock column to in_stock, then show the name and in_stock columns for the first 5 shoes.
hints: Three steps chained together: rename, then pick columns, then head().

solution_lines.explain: Rename with a dictionary: old name to new name.
Pick two columns, using the NEW name.

recap: Level 1 complete! You can load a dataset, size it up, pick the columns you need, and use lists and dictionaries, on any CSV file.
